Police obtained security footage from a nearby liquor store showing the victim being approached by 29-year-old Randy Rinaldo Schillingford. The 12-year-old victim was trailing behind his 13-year-old brother who told police he ran ahead to use the bathroom at a CVS down the road. Both were spending their night at the Margate Fair. Over the next several minutes, Randy appears to grapple and drag the 12-year-old dozens of yards away. Bystanders and civilian vehicles pass by, possibly unaware of the seriousness behind what is happening. After being pulled about 100 yards, the victim breaks free and runs north towards CVS. Randy initially stays nearby, then begins walking in the opposite direction. He is then caught on camera receiving vigilante justice from what officials called a Good Samaritan. Seconds later, police arrive on the scene. The Margate Fair has drawn controversy in recent years for its allegedly rising criminal activity, with some believing this is due to it being open late at night and attracting a bad crowd. Reports indicate that in recent years the fair has seen children pepper spray, overdoses requiring Narcan, a carnival worker arrested as a sex offender, a fair worker accused of selling drugs, reports of 500 juveniles clogging parking lots, and shots of unidentified gun fire. In a separate incident, a carnival worker fired a gun and struck a 91-year-old woman in the foot at a nearby assisted living facility. Police Major Kevin Stransky of the Margate Police Department can be quoted saying, if we continue to host these carnivals, I fear that it isn't if, but when, that something potentially tragic will happen to either one of our officers or someone in the public. Months before this night, the town debated closing the fare by 10 o'clock with town commissioner Arlene Schwartz stating that nothing good happens at that time. Post from late 2025 show the fair stays open until one in the morning on some nights, indicating no permanent changes were made. Unsurprisingly, the incident in this video occurred shortly past 10 o'clock. After his arrest, Randy was charged with one count of kidnapping a child under the age of 13, one count of lewd or lascivious conduct towards a minor, one count of robbery, likely due to the victim reporting Randy kept trying to take his bracelets and one count of battery. State prosecutors moved forward with defining Randy as a career criminal due to his previous charges in recent years, which include one count of robbery, seven counts trespassing, two counts resisting, two counts aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, two counts of threatening a public servant, two counts possession of cannabis, six counts of battery, one count of disorderly intoxication, and two counts of criminal mischief. Randy was held with no bond and pled not guilty. Eleven months later, he changed his plea to Nolo Contenderay, meaning he did not admit guilt, but agreed to proceed as if he were guilty. The state also changed his charges prior to sentencing, likely due to a plea deal. Kidnapping was changed to false imprisonment, dropping the severity from a first to third-degree felony. Lude conduct towards a minor and strong-arm robbery were both altered to child abuse, going from second to third-degree felonies, and his charge for battery remained. Randy was sentenced to five years in prison with 336 days of jail credit, assuming he serves a full sentence, he will not be released until December of 2027.
